subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What private/ephemeral session guarantee should OpenClaw support before implementation: hard no-read/no-write/no-history, a narrower context-only demo mode, or no user-facing privacy guarantee?
rationale: This cannot be decided mechanically because the feature defines a user-visible privacy boundary spanning protocol, persisted state, memory, tools, channels, UI, plugin APIs, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Hard Ephemeral Contract
options.body: Add an enforced per-session/per-channel private mode that blocks private context reads and durable transcript, memory, plugin, tool, and artifact writes, with visible UI status and regression tests.

options.title: Context-Only Demo Mode
options.body: Ship a narrower mode that suppresses bootstrap/workspace context but explicitly avoids promising no session or memory persistence.

options.title: Decline Core Privacy Mode
options.body: Close the core request if OpenClaw will not promise a no-persistence session boundary, and document supported cleanup or plugin-only alternatives instead.

recommendation.title: Hard Ephemeral Contract
recommendation.body: Add an enforced per-session/per-channel private mode that blocks private context reads and durable transcript, memory, plugin, tool, and artifact writes, with visible UI status and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the freshest memory-flush/session-path history and already framed this issue as the canonical privacy-mode design tracker.
